\title{The Wrong Unit of Uncertainty:\\
Adaptive Design-Aware Conformal Inference for\\
Repeated Cross-National Surveys}
\author{The Authors}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Comparative research routinely reads a single wave-pair mean contrast and narrates it
as a persistent, distribution-wide, country-level trend---attaching uncertainty to the
wrong unit and over-detecting change. We give a principled instrument and a deployable
procedure: a finite-sample simultaneous band over a country's whole attitude
\emph{trajectory}, with the country as the exchangeable unit and a hierarchy of claims
(pairwise $\to$ any-pair $\to$ net $\to$ persistent country-wide) whose top rung is the
honest object. The band is a clustered conformal band exact at any $K$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:exact}) inside a selector that corrects for survey design only when it
can be certified reliable and otherwise abstains, provably correctly
(Theorem~\ref{thm:safe}). Applied to real data it changes the substantive picture: in the
ESS (2018--2022), persistent distribution-wide trust decline is certified in one of
roughly thirty democracies (Greece), not the twenty flagged marginally; on the World
Values Survey (1981--2022) the marginal case for Foa--Mounk ``deconsolidation''
over-counts the persistent phenomenon by $2.6$--$6.5\times$. A second, subtler error---the
calibration objects, other countries' distributions, are themselves estimated from
complex samples---we resolve by mapping its scope: correcting for it is non-identified
without the design-noise law (Theorem~\ref{thm:impossible}) and, even with it, unreachable
below $K\ge94$ exchangeable populations (Proposition~\ref{prop:unreach}), so the
abstaining reduction is the right object at survey scale rather than a concession.
\end{abstract}

\section{Proofs and efficiency results}\label{app:proofs}
Full statements and proofs of Theorems~\ref{thm:impossible}--\ref{thm:safe}, the
efficiency results AW-1--AW-3, the open excess-width oracle inequality, and the
modulation self-inclusion deficit are collected in the supplementary theory notes
(\texttt{docs/THEORY\_MAIN.md}, \texttt{docs/DESIGN\_AWARE\_THEOREM.md},
\texttt{docs/ADAPTIVE\_WIDTH\_THEORY.md}). Each theorem has a machine-checked contract
test (\texttt{tests/test\_theorem0.py}, \texttt{test\_deconv\_safe.py},
\texttt{test\_safe\_selector.py}).

\section{Frozen selector specification and validation protocol}\label{app:spec}
The frozen constants ($\rho_0=0.47$, $\delta_{\max}=0.02$,
$\widehat\delta_{\text{UCB}}(D)=0.0061+0.0943\,D$, $g_{\min}=0.10$, margin
$\Delta_g=0.05$, stability floor) and their derivation on the development grid are in
\texttt{docs/SAFE\_SELECTOR\_SPEC.md}. The sealed independent-validation
preregistration, grid, and seed manifest are in
\texttt{docs/INDEPENDENT\_VALIDATION\_PREREG.md} and \texttt{configs/}; results in
\texttt{docs/HOLDOUT\_VALIDATION\_RESULTS.md}.

\section*{Data and Code Availability}
All simulation, theory, and benchmark results in this paper are deterministic: they run
under fixed random seeds and reproduce exactly with no external data. Each theorem is
paired with a machine-checked contract test that verifies its stated guarantee
numerically. The ESS, World Values Survey, and AmericasBarometer/LAPOP microdata used in
the reanalyses are licensed to their respective providers and are not redistributed here;
the replication package documents the exact variables, waves, and retrieval steps needed
to obtain them directly from each provider. The full replication package---code for the
method, all simulations and theorem contract tests, and the analysis pipeline---will be
deposited in the Political Analysis Dataverse (Harvard Dataverse) upon conditional
acceptance.
